summary: toLowerCase returns a new string with letters converted using Unicode default lowercase mappings.
documentation: toLowerCase returns a new string with letters converted using Unicode default lowercase mappings. The source string stays unchanged. It is useful for agreed case-insensitive identifiers when the identifier grammar is defined separately.
inputs: An array of ASCII tag strings.
returns: Lowercase strings in the original order.
caution: Lowercasing does not trim text, remove punctuation or perform Unicode normalization. Locale-sensitive naming may need toLocaleLowerCase and a clear locale policy.
scenarios: Normalize agreed ASCII status labels before comparison.
Create uniform internal tag labels from imported rows.
Make case-insensitive local search keys for ASCII codes.
title: Normalize ASCII tags
problem: Return a new array with each ASCII input string lowercased. Keep whitespace, punctuation, duplicates and ordering unchanged.
hint: Map the method over the strings without adding trim.
goal: Use String.toLowerCase() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
